ambiguities.description: Open ambiguities this step could not settle; each names what it is about. An item is deleted once its answer is applied.

fixtures.description: Array of test fixtures. A fixture is a verifier: it gives a concrete input and expected result that proves one or more spec nodes. It names what it proves in `verifies` (an acceptance criterion, an API, an invariant or an NFR), or, for a removal fixture, in `removes` (the id of a deleted node whose behaviour must be gone). Example: fix-auth-login-success verifies ac-user-login-1 and the success response contract of api-auth-login. A fixture names no test and no command; the binding to a test is a verification record. Anti-pattern: a fixture that verifies nothing.

items.description: A single test fixture with input data, expected output, testing mode, and the nodes it verifies. Fixtures are the executable contracts between spec and implementation. A fixture must name what it proves: at least one of verifies or removes.

fixture_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this fixture. Naming convention: fix-{feature}-{scenario}-{mode-suffix-optional}. Examples: 'fix-auth-login-success' (happy path unit test), 'fix-auth-login-invalid-e2e' (end-to-end invalid credentials test), 'fix-payment-duplicate-redteam' (adversarial duplicate payment test). Should be stable across spec versions — renaming breaks traceability links. Anti-pattern: 'fix-1', 'fix-test-001' (sequential labels with no traceable meaning).

description.description: Human-readable description of what this fixture tests. Format: 'Given [precondition], when [action], then [expected outcome].' Example: 'Given a user account with email alice@example.com exists and email_verified=true, when POST /auth/login is called with correct credentials, then a 200 response with a JWT token is returned within 200ms.' Alternative format: '{fr-id or target}: {scenario} → {expected outcome}'. Examples: 'fr-user-login: valid credentials submitted → 200 OK with session_token in response body', 'api-payment-charge: amount exceeds account balance → 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS error with retry guidance'. Anti-pattern: 'Tests login' (no precondition, action, or expected outcome); 'FR-03 login test' — use the kebab-case fr-id format (not FR-03 number format) and include the expected outcome.

verifies.description: Ids of the nodes this fixture proves: acceptance criteria (step 04), APIs (step 05), invariants (step 06) or NFRs (step 07). Not functional requirements: a functional requirement is proven through its criteria. Example: ["ac-user-login-1", "api-auth-login"]. An API error is not listed here: name it in `expects`. A fixture must carry verifies or removes.

expects.description: Id of the API error (step 05) this fixture expects as its outcome. At most one. Not a proof: an API error is proven through the criterion it derives from, so `expects` does not make anything verified. Give the error's `http_status` as `expected.status` when you name it. Example: ["err-auth-token-expired"] with expected {"status": 410, "body": {"error": "token-expired"}}. Anti-pattern: naming an error here and a different status in `expected`; listing an error in `verifies`.

removes.description: Ids of deleted nodes whose behaviour this fixture proves is gone (for example an endpoint that now answers 404). The fixture is justified by the removed id; the id need not exist any more. Optional.

mode.description: Testing mode that determines how this fixture is executed. Decision rules: 'unit' — test a single function or validation rule in complete isolation with all dependencies mocked, no network calls; 'contract' — test the request/response boundary at the API layer, service dependencies mocked but the HTTP handler is live (use when the fixture verifies an API); 'e2e' — test a full user journey across integrated components where the service layer is real (use when the fixture verifies a criterion that spans multiple components); 'manual' — a person follows written steps; manual_reason is then required; 'redteam' — adversarial inputs designed to trigger security, data-integrity, or business-logic violations. For a user-login criterion: unit mode tests the JWT signing logic in isolation (all HTTP mocked); contract mode tests the POST /auth/login endpoint with auth service mocked; e2e mode tests the full login flow including DB and session store; redteam mode tests alg:none JWT attack and SQL injection in the email field. Anti-pattern: using 'unit' for a fixture that verifies an API — those should be 'contract' or 'e2e'.

input.description: The input data used to set up this fixture's test scenario. Should be concrete and realistic — use representative values that reflect actual production data shapes. Include: required fields, boundary values, and any data that triggers the specific behavior being tested. Good: {"email": "alice@example.com", "password": "hunter2"} (real-looking, domain-specific). Bad: {"email": "test", "password": "test"} (not representative of real data) or {"data": {...}} (wrapped in unnecessary envelope). Use realistic but non-PII data. Avoid: generic placeholder values ('foo', 'test123'), incomplete objects, or data that doesn't reflect the real system's constraints.

expected.description: The expected system behavior after applying the input. Each outcome should be: (1) specific — reference exact field names, status codes, or system states; (2) verifiable — an engineer should be able to write an assertion from this; (3) complete — cover all observable effects of the operation. Example: 'Response status 201, response body contains user_id and auth_token, database record created with correct email hash'. When the outcome is an API error named in `expects`, `expected.status` equals the `http_status` of that error.

tags.description: Array of short labels for categorising and filtering fixtures in CI. At least one tag recommended. Standard tags to consider: 'smoke' (run on every commit), 'regression' (run on PR), 'performance' (load/stress tests), 'security' (auth/authz coverage), 'slow' (tests that take >5s). Example: ["auth", "critical", "pii"]. CI pipeline runs --tags critical for pre-merge gates and --tags auth for auth-service-specific test suites. Each tag must match the pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$. Anti-pattern: more than 5 tags per fixture — over-tagging reduces the value of tag-based filtering. Anti-pattern: custom tags that are never filtered on in CI — tags only add value when pipeline configuration uses them.

items.description: A short categorisation label. Use lowercase letters, digits, dots, colons, and hyphens only. Examples: 'smoke', 'regression', 'security', 'slow', 'env:prod-only', 'fr:user-login'. Colon-separated tags (env:, fr:) create namespaced categories. Anti-pattern: spaces or uppercase (use dots/colons as separators, not spaces); avoid tags longer than 20 characters.

tag_ref.description: Canonical reference to a tag defined in the canonical registry. Required for every fixture. Kind is structurally pinned to 'tag'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:tag:critical-path", "kind": "tag", "label": "critical-path"}. Always populate tag_ref with the primary canonical tag for this fixture. If the appropriate tag is not yet in the canon registry, add it there first using 'specdev canon-accept' before authoring this fixture.

manual_reason.description: Why this check cannot be automated. Required when mode is 'manual', where input and expected describe the procedure and the observable result. Example: 'The printed receipt layout is judged by a person; no automated oracle exists'.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this fixture: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this fixture; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

derives_from.description: Ids of the seeds this fixture takes content from directly. Optional: list a seed routed to this step, and only for content taken straight from the seed and not through an upstream node.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this fixture replaces. Optional.

allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).
